held_because: real finding not applicable (quote found 0x): set a phalanx of passions against pleasure
source:
∆ειλὸς στρατιώτης
ἐκλύει πολεμιστῶν χεῖρας καὶ ἀμελὴς μοναχὸς χαυνοῖ προθυμίαν ἀδελφῶν. Σμῆνος μελισσῶν ἐργάζεται κηρίον καὶ σύστημα ἀδελφῶν βασιλείαν οὐρανῶν. Σάλπιγξ διεγείρει προθυμίαν πολεμιστῶν καὶ μαθητῶν σπουδὴν διδασκαλία πρακτικῆς ἀρετῆς. Ὅπλισον †δακτύλων λόγοις, ἡγούμενε, σοὺς ἀδελφοὺς καὶ θωράκισον ἐπαγγελίαις τῶν μελλόντων ἀγαθῶν· φράξον θυρεῷ πίστεως ἄθλοις καὶ περικνήμισον ἐλπίδι τῇ εἰς τὸν θεόν· †κήνησον τοὺς πόδας ἐν εὐαγγελικοῖς μαθήμασι καὶ ζῶσον τὴν ὀσφὺν σωφροσύνης λόγοις· δὸς μάχαιραν εἰς τὴν χεῖρα κατὰ τῶν παθῶν ὀξύτατον θυμὸν καὶ ἀντίταξον φάλαγγα παθῶν ἡδονῇ.
english: A cowardly soldier makes the hands of warriors go slack, and a careless monk drains the eagerness of his brothers. A swarm of bees produces a honeycomb, and a community of brothers produces the kingdom of heaven. A trumpet rouses the eagerness of warriors, and teaching in active virtue rouses the zeal of disciples. Arm your brothers, leader, with words [the Greek here is corrupt: "of fingers"], and put on them the breastplate of the promises of good things to come. Fence them with the shield of faith in struggles, and put greaves on them with hope in God. Shoe their feet [the printed verb is corrupt; "shoe" is a conjecture] with the lessons of the gospel, and gird their loins with words of self-control. Put into their hand the sharpest anger as a sword against the passions, and set a phalanx of the passions against pleasure.

findings.checker_says: δακτύλων means 'fingers', not 'ten commandments'; corrupted text misread as δεκάλογος
findings.reviewer_note: Stale: English already reads 'words of your fingers'. The source word is cruxed (†δακτύλων), so any rendering is provisional.

findings.checker_says: κήνησον means 'move/stir,' not 'shod.' The command is to move or stir the feet, not to put shoes on them.
findings.reviewer_note: †κήνησον is cruxed; 'shoe' (ὑπόδησον, cf. Eph 6:15 armor sequence) is the sensible emendation. Only nit: imperative should be 'Shoe', not 'Shod'.

findings.quote: set a phalanx of passions against pleasure
findings.checker_says: ἡδονῇ is dative of means/instrument, not opponent; means 'with pleasure' or 'for pleasure', not 'against pleasure'
findings.reviewer_note: ἀντιτάσσω + dat. = array against; Evagrius sets the irascible against pleasure. Checker's 'instrumental' claim is wrong, and the repair made it worse: current English 'against them with pleasure' must revert.
